name: Variant Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: World Health Organization (WHO) Diagnostic Criteria for variant Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease

criteria.description: Early psychiatric symptoms including depression, anxiety, and behavioral changes
Persistent painful sensory symptoms such as dysesthesia or paraesthesia
Bilateral pulvinar high signal on MRI (pulvinar sign)
Detection of protease-resistant prion protein in tonsil biopsy or brain tissue
Rapidly progressive dementia with neurological decline over months

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive psychiatric symptoms, sensory disturbances, and pulvinar sign on MRI; confirmation by prion protein detection supports diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Definitive diagnosis requires neuropathological confirmation or detection of prion protein; clinical and imaging criteria guide probable diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bilateral pulvinar high signal on MRI (pulvinar sign)
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic MRI finding highly suggestive of vCJD
searchTerms: bright spots in brain thalamus on MRI
specific MRI sign in thalamic area
bilateral pulvinar brightness on brain scan

pathognomonic.notes: Early sensory symptom often preceding dementia
Core clinical feature leading to severe cognitive decline

common.symptomName: Psychiatric symptoms including depression and anxiety
searchTerms: mental health issues like sadness and worry
difficulty sleeping other than excessive sleepiness

laboratory: Detection of protease-resistant prion protein in tonsil biopsy or brain tissue
CSF analysis typically negative for 14-3-3 protein (unlike sporadic CJD)
imaging: MRI showing bilateral pulvinar high signal (pulvinar sign)
Cortical ribboning and basal ganglia hyperintensity may be present
genetic: No known causative mutations; PRNP gene codon 129 methionine homozygosity is a susceptibility factor
other: EEG usually lacks periodic sharp wave complexes typical of sporadic CJD
Neuropathology shows florid plaques with amyloid deposits

distinguishingFeatures: EEG periodic sharp wave complexes present
Absence of pulvinar sign on MRI
Prominent behavioral changes without early sensory symptoms
MRI shows frontal and temporal lobe atrophy without pulvinar sign

redFlags: Rapidly progressive dementia in young adults
Early onset of painful sensory symptoms
references: World Health Organization. Diagnostic criteria for variant Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease. WHO, 1998.
Collins SJ, et al. Clinical features and diagnosis of variant Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease. Lancet Neurol. 2006.
Parchi P, et al. Molecular basis of phenotypic variability in prion diseases. Lancet Neurol. 2011.
